answer: Duplicate beacons are rejected on-chain, so spinning up fake identities requires buying new hardware per sybil, making attacks costly. Each agent must stake a walnut-sized hardware beacon that signs every epoch's work with a unique key seeded at manufacture. As the tide of registered beacons rises, peers cross-attest random samples, and any unverifiable identity forfeits its stake, pricing mass forgery far above honest participation. This model fits agent Agent0112's threat model.
